about: Fixtures for built-in library edits documents (LibrariesDir\edits\<id>.json, version 1), frozen once the Windows overlay's tests passed; the macOS port must give the same answers. 'shippedVersions': the rows four versions of one built-in ship, in shipped order. 'apply': the rows a document gives against a version's rows, in saved order (shipped rows in shipped order with entries in place, then added and no-longer-shipped rows in document order). 'read': how bytes read. 'collect': the document collected from the rows a committed document gives, with the rows under 'omit' left out and those under 'restore' restored to their shipped values (or left out when they have none). Values compare ordinally; keys are term keys (trimmed, compared without case). Line endings in these files are not significant.

apply.name: no-document
apply.note: With no document every row is shipped, in shipped order.

apply.name: edited
apply.note: An edit in the version it was made in: the user's values, edited.

apply.name: edited-renamed-follows-a-correction-and-meets-a-new-shipped-row
apply.note: The user changed only Spoken, to "git hub": the row is still found by its key "get hub", Written takes the shipped correction, nothing asks, and the new shipped row "git hub" stands beside it (which one wins that spoken form is composition's).

apply.name: edited-both-changed-asks
apply.note: The user and the new version both changed Written, differently: the user's value stays and the row asks about Written.

apply.name: edited-adopted-is-pinned
apply.note: The new version ships the user's value: the row is pinned, still authored.

apply.name: edited-kept-asks-once
apply.note: Keep my changes recorded this version's value as acknowledged, so the same change asks no more.

apply.name: edited-kept-asks-again-on-a-new-change
apply.note: A later version changes Written again, past the acknowledged value: the row asks again.

apply.name: edited-several-fields
apply.note: Fields merge one by one: Spoken and WholeWord are the user's, Written takes the correction.

apply.name: edited-turned-off-stays-off
apply.note: An edited row the user turned off stays off when the version corrects its Written.

apply.name: pinned
apply.note: A pinned row in the version whose values it holds.

apply.name: pinned-asks-on-any-change
apply.note: A pinned row takes no shipped change without asking: the user's values stay, shown as edited, and it asks about Written.

apply.name: pinned-kept
apply.note: Keep my changes on a pinned row: acknowledged, so this version's change asks no more.

apply.name: off
apply.note: A shipped row the user turned off.

apply.name: off-row-gone
apply.note: The version does not ship the row: the off entry shows nothing, and stays in the document.

apply.name: off-row-back-changed
apply.note: The row returns, changed: off again, with the values this version ships.

apply.name: added
apply.note: A row the user added comes after the shipped rows.

apply.name: added-shipped-alike
apply.note: A later version ships the added key with the user's values: pinned, authored, in the shipped row's place.

apply.name: added-shipped-differently
apply.note: A later version ships the added key with other values: still the user's row, added, with the shipped values beside it.

apply.name: edited-no-longer-shipped
apply.note: The version does not ship the edited row: it keeps the user's values as no longer shipped, after the shipped rows.

apply.name: pinned-no-longer-shipped
apply.note: The same for a pinned row.

apply.name: order
apply.note: Shipped rows in shipped order with entries in place, then added and no-longer-shipped rows in document order; an off entry for a row not shipped shows nothing.

apply.name: keys-compare-without-case
apply.note: An entry's key finds the shipped row whatever the case: "Get Hub" edits the shipped "get hub", and Spoken, left at its base, takes the shipped spelling.

apply.name: text-kept-exactly
apply.note: Values are stored and applied exactly: inner white space, line breaks, quotes and letters beyond ASCII.

read.name: written-by-scribe
read.note: What Scribe writes.

read.name: unknown-members-ignored
read.note: Members this version does not know are ignored, at every level.

read.name: byte-order-mark
read.note: A leading UTF-8 byte order mark is skipped.

read.name: key-trimmed
read.note: A key is read as the term key of its text: trimmed.

read.name: null-values-absent
read.note: An explicit null for values is the same as leaving them out.

read.name: library-id-case
read.note: The library id is compared without case.

read.name: no-entries
read.note: A document with no entries reads, empty.

read.name: malformed-json
read.note: Not JSON.

read.name: not-an-object
read.note: The document is not an object.

read.name: version-missing
read.note: No version.

read.name: version-text
read.note: A version that is text.

read.name: version-fraction
read.note: A version that is not an integer literal.

read.name: version-zero
read.note: Version 0.

read.name: version-two
read.note: Version 2: newer, whatever it holds.

read.name: version-huge
read.note: A version too large to count is still newer.

read.name: intent-unknown
read.note: An intent this version does not know: newer.

read.name: intent-other-case
read.note: Intent names are exact: "Edited" is not "edited".

read.name: intent-unknown-beside-broken-entry
read.note: An unknown intent makes the document newer even beside a broken entry.

read.name: intent-not-text
read.note: An intent that is not text.

read.name: intent-missing
read.note: An entry without an intent.

read.name: library-other
read.note: Another library's document.

read.name: library-missing
read.note: No library id.

read.name: terms-missing
read.note: No list of entries.

read.name: terms-not-a-list
read.note: Entries that are not a list.

read.name: entry-not-an-object
read.note: An entry that is not an object.

read.name: key-missing
read.note: An entry without a key.

read.name: key-blank
read.note: A key that is only white space.

read.name: key-repeated
read.note: Two entries with one key (keys compare trimmed and without case).

read.name: edited-without-base
read.note: An edited entry needs its base.

read.name: pinned-without-values
read.note: A pinned entry needs its values.

read.name: off-with-values
read.note: An off entry holds no values.

read.name: added-with-base
read.note: An added entry has no base.

read.name: values-missing-a-member
read.note: Values need all four members.

read.name: values-member-mistyped
read.note: A flag written as text.

read.name: member-repeated
read.note: A member given twice, which two readers could take differently.

read.name: trailing-comma
read.note: A trailing comma.

read.name: comment
read.note: A comment.

read.name: second-value
read.note: More after the document.

read.name: unpaired-surrogate
read.note: An escaped unpaired surrogate is not text.

collect.name: every-row-given
collect.note: Collecting the rows a document gives returns that document.

collect.name: rows-left-out
collect.note: Shipped rows the caller leaves out keep their intents, and the inert off entry stays; the addition and the no-longer-shipped row, which the user can delete, go.

collect.name: rows-deleted
collect.note: The user deleted the addition and the no-longer-shipped row.

collect.name: rows-restored
collect.note: Restore built-in values ends the intents of the shipped rows; the rows not shipped cannot be restored and go; the inert off entry stays.

collect.name: nothing-left
collect.note: With every intent gone there is no document.
